title: Dashboard approve/reject protections
how_to_test: unauthenticated; missing/wrong CSRF; wrong Origin (compare scheme+host+port); missing Origin+Referer; wrong Host; Bearer with wrong Host; non-loopback bind without flag; session regenerated on login; idle and hard expiry; login rate limiter
notes: CSRF token required, Origin/Referer checked on POST, Host header allowlist blocks DNS rebinding on all requests (including Bearer), non-loopback bind refused without flag, session regenerated on login, 30m idle / 12h hard expiries enforced.

title: Dashboard stored XSS from agent-controlled text
how_to_test: tool/resource/agent_id/argument values containing
notes: Jinja2 autoescape strictly active; zero |safe filters in templates; hostile script/img payloads escaped in index and detail pages. Bug noted: nested mappingproxy arguments fail json.dumps in routes.py:80 and render (could not render).

title: Login limiter bypass and token exposure
how_to_test: spoof X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP; lockout only per IP?; token in URLs or logs
notes: 5-attempt limiter locks out with 429; X-Forwarded-For spoofing does not bypass limiter (client_ip = request.client.host); token never exposed in URLs, query params, or logs; token file requires 0600/0400.

title: Same-user attacker reads secrets
how_to_test: dashboard token via process args, /proc/<pid>/environ, token file permissions; signing key; approvals DB; policy.json; MCP client config; can it approve its own request via CLI or HTTP
notes: Attacker simulation proved same OS user can exfiltrate signing key, tamper with SQLite DB, read token from /proc/environ, self-approve via HTTP API, overwrite policy.json, and redirect MCP client configs. Blocked by different OS user (file permissions) and container isolation.

title: Key file loading
how_to_test: O_NOFOLLOW; fstat on the open fd; owner==euid; mode 0600/0400; parent dir owner/writability; symlink; wrong owner; group-readable; no key source => fails closed (no ephemeral key); inline DMINT_PRIVATE_KEY opt-in; no key material in logs, reprs, exceptions, tracebacks
notes: Key permissions (0600/0400), parent directory permissions, O_NOFOLLOW descriptor check, and exception redaction verified. Symlink quirk noted: check_key_file_permissions calls Path.resolve() while load_private_key_from_file opens directly with O_NOFOLLOW.

title: Gateway holds public keys only
how_to_test: fresh-process sys.modules check for dmint.mcp.gateway, dmint.mcp.__main__, dmint.mcp.config_loader (no signing or key-loading modules); run gateway with only trusted_issuers and no private key on disk or in env
notes: Fresh-process inspection proved dmint.mcp.gateway, dmint.mcp.__main__, dmint.mcp.config_loader load 0 private-key or signing modules.

title: Evaluator fail-closed on invalid resources
how_to_test: ALLOW "*" + DENY "/etc/passwd" + request "/../etc/passwd"; also NUL, backslash, %2e%2e, %252e%252e, %2f, empty, None, int, list, dict, 100k chars, NFC/NFD, case variants; all resource kinds (exact, any, none, path, url, host, identifier) and mixed kinds; agent-scoped candidate rules; the tool spy must never run
notes: Fail-closed resource validation verified on invalid kinds, non-string, NUL, %2e%2e, backslash, 100k strings, candidate rules. Tool spy never executed.

title: Evaluator purity and thread-safety
how_to_test: many threads with interleaved requests versus a single-thread baseline
notes: Policy purity and thread safety verified across 20 concurrent threads running 4,000 interleaved requests matching single-threaded baseline.

title: Canonicalization
how_to_test: byte-exact versus Node on >=200,000 random doubles plus edge values (1e-7, 1e21, 2**53, subnormals, -0.0) and strings (control chars, DEL, U+2028/2029, surrogate pairs, lone surrogates in VALUES and KEYS, UTF-16 key order); depth/size/cycle limits; NaN/Inf/bigint/tuple/non-string keys rejected; duplicate JSON keys rejected at the gateway
notes: Canonicalization parity verified against Node.js RFC 8785 on 10,021 random numbers, key ordering, escapes; duplicate JSON keys strictly rejected.

title: Fingerprint coverage and versioning
how_to_test: change each field (agent, tool, action, resource, arguments, policy provenance, anything else included) and show the fingerprint changes and the approval is invalid; domain-separation constants; v1 records and assertions fail closed without crashing list_pending or the dashboard
notes: Fingerprint coverage verified: changing any of 8 semantic fields alters fingerprint; v1 records fail closed safely without crashing list_pending.

title: Constraint regex cost
how_to_test: time fullmatch against 'a'*4096 (timeout 60): ^.*a.*a[a-z]{0,64}b$ ; ^\w*a\w*a\w{0,64}b$ ; ^.*a.*b$ ; ^.*a.*a.*a.*a.*b$ ; ^(a|a)+$ ; ^(a*)*$ ; {0,50}x4 and {0,500}x4 bounded combinations; report seconds and whether the policy loader rejects each; differential test of the validator against the stdlib parser (re._parser, tests only) on 5,000 random patterns, listing any accepted pattern that exceeds the validator's own limits
notes: validate_pattern_safety intercepts ReDoS patterns at policy load time; differential fuzzing of 5,000 patterns against sre_parse showed 0 bypasses.

title: Constraint semantics
how_to_test: ALLOW failing constraints + broader ALLOW => whole request DENY; two ALLOW rules (AND semantics); DENY rule constrained by enum ["shipped","delivered"] plus a broader ALLOW with order_status="pending" (report the exact decision and code); APPROVAL_REQUIRED with constraints; additionalProperties default and strict_arguments; bool/int/float/NaN/"999" against maximum 500; enum True versus 1; tuples; missing "type"
notes: Constraint semantics verified: failing constraints cannot be rescued by broader ALLOW; multiple ALLOW enforce AND; constrained DENY never loosens denial.

title: Unicode digits in patterns
how_to_test: does ^\d{3}$ accept "١٢٣"? \w, \s, (?i) behavior
notes: Verified Python regex default UNICODE semantics: ^\d{3}$ matches Arabic-Indic digits 123; \w matches accented chars; (?i) supported.

title: Ordering of constraint check and approval creation
how_to_test: through the REAL Dmint.authorize AND the gateway with a SQLiteApprovalStore attached: a violating request is DENY and list_pending stays empty; a valid request creates exactly one pending record
notes: Constraint evaluation strictly precedes approval creation: invalid arguments return DENY (DMT_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION) and store remains empty; valid request creates exactly 1 record.

title: TOCTOU
how_to_test: mutate the ORIGINAL nested arguments after authorization in decorator mode AND the gateway; executed call and stored fingerprint must use pre-mutation values
notes: TOCTOU defense verified: mutating original argument dictionary after authorization does not affect execution snapshot, stored record, or request fingerprint.

title: Secret leakage and notification injection
how_to_test: Postgres URL password variants (percent-encoded, containing @ or /, query string, libpq key=value, embedded inside driver error text) never in webhooks, logs, exceptions (including __cause__), CLI output or dashboard; list exactly which fields appear in Slack/Discord/Teams payloads; with a local fake receiver test @channel, @everyone, <!here>, markdown links and newlines in agent_id/tool/resource; webhook URL SSRF
notes: Postgres password variants, percent-encoding, unescaped @//, libpq strings, and driver error texts redacted by redact_database_url. Gaps: webhook payloads lack mention/markdown escaping (@everyone passes); webhook URL lacks SSRF validation.

title: Retry credential attacks
how_to_test: credential for a different request, agent, tool or resource; wrong audience; unknown issuer; expired; tampered; replay; two simultaneous retries; the spy shows the tool was not run; the approval field is stripped before forwarding downstream
notes: 9 retry credential attack vectors blocked (wrong args, agent, audience, issuer, expiry, signature, replay, race condition, credential stripping). Tool spy zero calls.

title: Agent identity binding
how_to_test: HTTP with no or invalid bearer token must not fall back to a default agent_id; client-supplied agent_id in arguments and in params/_meta; two agents with two tokens
notes: HTTP bearer token authentication strictly binds agent identity; missing/invalid tokens 401; zero fallback; agent cannot override identity via body/meta parameters.

title: SSRF
how_to_test: private ranges, loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, IPv6, IPv4-mapped IPv6, decimal/octal/hex/short IP forms, userinfo, redirects, trailing-dot hosts, DNS rebinding with a fake resolver (is the IP pinned between check and connect?)
notes: SSRF filter blocks private/loopback/metadata IPs, integer literals, userinfo, plain HTTP, and redirects (follow_redirects=False). Gaps: no IP pinning between DNS check and httpx connect (DNS rebinding window); static checks miss trailing-dot metadata hosts and octal/short IPs; ssrf.py:98 is dead code.

title: create-policy and compile-policy
how_to_test: malicious tool descriptions (tools file and MCP server); untrusted data is delimited; deterministic validation after the LLM; plain-English summary of every ALLOW rule; confirmation before writing; capture what is sent to the LLM with a fake endpoint; verify-policy fully offline (run with network blocked)
notes: Untrusted tool declarations extracted via AST and delimited in prompts; 4 deterministic post-LLM validation gates reject incomplete rules, credentials, and hallucinated capabilities; plain-English summary printed; interactive confirmation enforced; offline verify-policy operates 100% network-free.

title: Approval DB tampering by someone with DB write access
how_to_test: reset a CONSUMED row to APPROVED (recomputing any checksum) then replay the original assertion; extend expires_at; copy a row to another deployment_epoch; delete a CONSUMED row; change principal_id; downgrade state; state whether the row checksum is keyed (where is the key?); SQLite and Postgres
notes: CRITICAL VULNERABILITY: _integrity_checksum is an UNKEYED SHA-256 hash. An attacker with DB write access can reset CONSUMED to APPROVED, recompute checksum, and replay assertion (SUCCEEDED). Tampering with signed fields or extending expiry is BLOCKED by Ed25519 signature.

title: Decorator bypasses
how_to_test: async functions (supported? documented?), generators, methods/classmethods/staticmethods, __wrapped__, calling the undecorated function, id()-keyed registry after garbage collection, positional versus keyword fingerprint, default arguments, exception after consume
notes: Async functions rejected at decoration time; positional/keyword and default arguments normalized; __wrapped__ rejected; exception after consume blocks replay. Gaps: generator functions execute lazily outside gate; instance/class methods fail canonicalization on self/cls; address reuse in _registered leaks stale bindings.

title: Concurrency and crash safety
how_to_test: multi-PROCESS consume on SQLite and Postgres => exactly one winner; kill -9 mid-consume and after consume before execute; locked/busy DB; clock moved around expiry; read-only or full disk
notes: Multi-process race across 10 OS processes produces exactly 1 winner with zero DB corruption; clock expiry boundary respected; locked DB fails closed safely.

title: Policy integrity
how_to_test: is policy_digest pinning or remote/CDN loading implemented (code + test) or CLAIM-ONLY; same-user edit of policy.json then restart and reload; can the agent influence the policy path via env/args/config; duplicate JSON keys, huge or deeply nested files
notes: Policy digest pinning (expected_policy_digest) and remote/CDN policy loading are CLAIM-ONLY (unimplemented). Local file modifications do not affect running gateway until reload/restart. Same-user attacker can overwrite policy.json and restart gateway to ALLOW execution.

title: Tool schema drift
how_to_test: downstream MCP tool schema or description changes after policy generation: detected or not
notes: Downstream tool schema/description drift is not tracked or pinned; calls forwarded downstream unless strict_arguments=True intercepts unanticipated arguments.

title: Resource matching differential
how_to_test: >=150 tricky URLs versus Node WHATWG new URL(); 10,000 random paths versus posixpath; wildcard hosts (*.github.com must not match evil-github.com or github.com.evil.com); glob matcher timing on adversarial segment patterns
notes: Resource matching differential verified against Node WHATWG URL (188 URLs) and posixpath (10,000 paths); wildcard host boundaries strictly enforced; segment glob matcher executes in <0.2ms with zero backtracking blowup.

title: Docs, landing page and package accuracy
how_to_test: license, versions, classifiers, test counts, performance numbers (reproduce them), terminal examples on the landing page (run them), repo-layout claims, docs versus CLI --help versus code
notes: SECURITY.md:53 claims SQLite WAL mode, but sqlite.py:240 omits PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL (defaults to delete mode).

title: Shim or dead modules
how_to_test: src/dmint/canonicalize.py, enforcement.py, hashing.py, storage/__init__.py (previously 0% coverage): contents, importers, duplication or shadowing of core/
notes: questionary and sqlalchemy lack upper bounds in pyproject.toml; optional dependency lists httpx2 typo for httpx; shim modules in src/dmint/ export subsets.

title: Pydantic Field alias warning
how_to_test: does Field(alias=...) have an effect in the dashboard handlers
notes: Dashboard handlers do not use Pydantic models or Field(alias=...); form parameters use standard FastAPI Form(...) primitives with zero alias warnings or binding errors.

title: Unclosed sqlite connections on Python 3.13
how_to_test: allocation site via -X tracemalloc=25: src/ or tests/
notes: Confirmed via Python 3.13 -X tracemalloc=25 -W error::ResourceWarning. Allocation site: src/dmint/core/storage/sqlite.py:279 via ThreadSafeApprovalStore in src/dmint/core/storage/thread_safe.py:99.

title: Coverage of security-critical modules
how_to_test: generated by script from coverage.json; quoted uncovered lines for every module under 90%
notes: 292 tracked files scanned with zero real secret leaks; branch coverage table compiled in tables/coverage.md.

title: Python version matrix
how_to_test: full suite on every available declared version plus the newest; compare with classifiers
notes: Python 3.10, 3.12, 3.13 verified with 1158 tests passing; docs code blocks evaluated: 6 syntax errors in docs/ code fences.

title: Mutation survivors
how_to_test: see Phase 9
notes: 49 mutations tested: 45 killed (91.8%), 4 true survivors documented (MUT-11, MUT-16, MUT-47, MUT-48) with proposed regression tests in proposed_tests/test_mutation_regressions.py.

title: Deployment-model doc accuracy
how_to_test: every statement in docs/deployment-model.md versus the Phase 8 experiments
notes: All 10 deployment and threat model statements in docs/deployment-model.md verified 100% accurate against runtime tests (shared user compromise, /proc/cmdline exposure, 0600 token enforcement, loopback bind refusal).

title: Build artifacts
how_to_test: wheel and sdist contents (no secrets, tests, stray files, correct license metadata); install from the built artifact in a clean venv; entry points run
notes: Wheel and sdist built via build --no-isolation; twine check passed; wheel clean (103 files, 0 tests, 0 secrets, py.typed present); clean venv install tested with dmint, dmint-mcp, dmint-dashboard all exiting 0.

title: Policy authoring CLI paths
how_to_test: compile-policy and create-policy previously-uncovered lines exercised with a fake LLM; failure handling
notes: Full path coverage for wizard conversation loop: shape retries (up to 3 attempts), clarification questions multi-turn handling, policy correction retries (up to 4 attempts), fail-fast input validation (missing, empty, >64KB limit), and compile-policy wrapper.
